title: sse: fix streaming chunking and framing edge cases (partial JSON, delimiters, ordering)
author: Aisha Patel
body: Motivation: several customers and internal CI runs surfaced stability issues in the SSE/streaming path when payloads contain partial JSON tokens, custom delimiters, or when token/event ordering across batching causes out-of-order event boundaries. This PR fixes framing and chunking logic across the OpenAI-compat SSE adapter and the serving runtime framer. Changes include: 1) deterministic event boundary detection using byte-level state rather than token split heuristics; 2) improved handling for partial JSON objects across frames (keeps a compact prefix buffer and emits only when a full event is parsed or a safe flush threshold is hit); 3) consistent delimiter normalization so CRLF/CR/LF/mixed-line endings are treated uniformly; 4) reorder-safety guard for batched responses: we tag fragments with monotonic sequence IDs and reassemble per-connection before emitting; 5) added end-of-stream sentinel for compatibility with some OpenAI-like SSE clients. The description below summarizes the implementation, tests, and rollout plan. Implementation summary: updated redwood/openai_compat/sse_streaming.py to centralize chunk-state machine; added low-level framer in serving/runtime/streaming_framer.cc with a small state machine and unit-tested C++ path; normalized newline handling in SDK streaming clients (redwood-sdk-python/redwood/streams.py) to ensure clients interpret events the same as server; docs: updated redwood-docs/api/streaming.md with compatibility notes. Tests: added focused unit tests for partial JSON (tests/integration/test_sse_chunking.py) and an end-to-end canary that runs against the perf-canary harness. CI: flaky test caused an initial failure on 2024-11-09; fixed by tightening timeout and re-running; final CI green. Rollout/compat: this is backwards-compatible for most clients; the one notable change is stricter handling of CRLF vs LF delimiters which fixes failures but may change how some custom clients detect event boundaries. Rollout will be gradual: feature-flag off by default for Dedicated until rollout window. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for chunker and framer - [x] integration test exercising partial JSON + delimiter permutations - [x] docs update with migration notes - [x] perf smoke to verify no regression - [x] CI green on re-run

d4e5f6: python sdk newline normalization and client tests
f7g8h9: add integration tests for partial JSON and delimiter cases
files_changed: redwood/openai_compat/sse_streaming.py: centralizes SSE state machine; adds sequence-id tagging; normalizes CRLF/LF handling
serving/runtime/streaming_framer.cc: new C++ framer implementation with compact prefix buffer and flush heuristics
redwood-sdk-python/redwood/streams.py: normalize newline handling and expose client-side reassembly options
redwood-docs/api/streaming.md: document edge cases, migration notes, examples
tests/integration/test_sse_chunking.py: parametrized tests for partial json across chunks, mixed delimiters, and out-of-order fragments
review_comments: Luca Marin: Nice consolidation of state; can you add a short comment explaining why we choose a monotonic sequence id vs timestamps? Author reply: added comment in sse_streaming.py explaining ordering guarantees and why timestamps are insufficient for reassembly under heavy batching.

Priya Desai: CI flake repro looks like an edge-case with the perf harness. Can we add a test that simulates partial payloads with sleeps? Author reply: added a slow-producer variant to the integration tests and a perf-canary scenario.

Marcus Lee: Concern: will the stricter delimiter normalization break older clients that relied on multiple newlines? Author reply: documented the compatibility change in streaming.md and added a feature-flag for Dedicated to defer the behavior change during enterprise rollouts.
release_notes: Fix SSE streaming edge cases: partial JSON across frames, mixed delimiter handling (CRLF/LF), and out-of-order fragment reassembly. Improves streaming stability for OpenAI-compat clients; see streaming.md for migration notes.
